title: Al-Muqaddim, the Expediter
tomorrow: and when He puts something back, what then?

lines: IS THERE A NAME FOR THAT?
cards: There's a tab you've had open for weeks. An email you starred and never answered. A call you'll make right after this one thing.
Yesterday's question: is there a Name for that? There is, and it isn't a scolding. It's Al-Muqaddim, the Expediter, the one who brings forward.
And the clearest teaching on it came with a hand on someone's shoulder.

teach.b: Start with a prayer. In Sahih al-Bukhari, a du'a of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, ends by calling God the one who brings forward and the one who puts back. Two Names, side by side: today's, and tomorrow's.
In this picture, what arrives first is not random. A chance, a person, a moment, an opening: God brings it forward. The Qur'an speaks of time the same way.
Every people has its term, it says, and when the term comes, no one can put it back an hour or bring it forward. So what do you do with what's been brought forward? Here's the hand on the shoulder.
Abdullah ibn Umar tells it in Bukhari: the Prophet took hold of his shoulder and said, be in this world as if you were a stranger, or a traveler on the road. A traveler doesn't redecorate the inn.

And Ibn Umar turned it into advice of his own: when evening comes, don't wait for morning; when morning comes, don't wait for evening. Take from your health for your sickness, and from your life for your death.
That's the line to tell a friend tonight. It isn't panic.
It's noticing that what's in front of you today was brought forward on purpose, and that a road keeps moving.

how: Muslims who pray at night may use the Prophet's du'a that calls God the one who brings forward and the one who puts back; Ibn Umar's advice about evening and morning is often quoted in talks on using time well.

o: the one who brings forward what He wills
the one who hurries people into action
the one who knows what came before

games.q: who said what — tap the pairs.
p: how to be in this world

s: Al-Muqaddim is a Name about rushing
it's about God's order: what He brings forward, when He wills.
the Prophet told Ibn Umar to live like a traveler on the road
be in this world as if you were a stranger, or a traveler on the road.
the Prophet's du'a names al-Muqaddim beside another Name
the one who brings forward and the one who puts back: today's Name and tomorrow's.

games.q: your little brother says he'll start his science project 'when he's in the mood.' it's due friday. what would Ibn Umar tell him?
o: start one small piece now: when evening comes, don't wait for morning.
wait for the mood; work that's forced never turns out well.
do the whole thing tonight in one push, then forget about it.
games.why: Ibn Umar said: when evening comes, don't wait for morning. the point is what's in front of you now, not a heroic all-nighter.

practice: Bring the pushed-back thing to mind and shrink it to its first move: one sentence of the email, one box on the form, one text. If that move fits in a minute, make it now.
Then let the rest of the sit hold the difference between done and someday.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muqaddim. The Expediter: the one who brings forward whatever He wills, in His own order.

orig.note: Arabic: the Expediter, the one who brings forward. its partner Name is al-Mu'akhkhir.

carryVoice: Here's the line: brought forward, to you, today, on purpose, by the one who keeps the clock. Peace till tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6398 (the Prophet's du'a: 'You are the one who brings forward and You are the one who puts back'); also Sahih Muslim 2719
Qur'an 7:34 (every people has its term; it cannot be delayed an hour or brought forward)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6416 (be in this world as a stranger or a traveler; Ibn Umar: when evening comes, don't wait for morning)
